method: closed-form photon transport: Klein-Nishina energy-transfer fraction + Katz-Penfold CSDA range + <Z/A> mass energy-absorption ratio. Literature constants only; no DFT.

falsification_margin.note: The photoelectric and pair channels are not computed. This is the share of total mass energy absorption they would have to supply in the ZIF (and ~none in water) for DEF to reach unity — the number a lab check would have to beat.

verdict: Physical radiosensitisation by the ZIF nanozyme is REJECTED at Co-60 1.25 MeV on two independent grounds. (1) Non-locality: the mean Compton electron is 588 keV with a 2.05 mm CSDA range, so every layer of the stack is a Bragg-Gray cavity (1e-02 of the range at most) whose dose is imposed by the surrounding medium; a local excess of interactions cannot raise it. (2) Coefficient direction: per unit mass Compton absorption tracks <Z/A>, which FALLS with Z, so even the all-Ce upper-bound node absorbs 0.858x water, not more. A non-Compton channel would have to supply 14.2% of the ZIF's total absorption to reach DEF 1.0, and would still have to beat (1). CONSEQUENCE: 01_04 6.3 Branch A stands as written - gamma on the LOADED anchor; aseptic loading after sterilisation is NOT required by this risk. RESIDUAL is chemical, not dosimetric (Fenton-like radiolysis on redox-active Ce/Cu/Co, sign open because the same nanozyme is SOD/catalase-like) and is measured by the Branch A activity assay already planned - run it with AND without the ZIF.
caveats: Hypothesis, not measurement (00_06 0). Closed-form transport with literature constants; ZIF node stoichiometry is NOT fixed by canon, so the sweep brackets it and quotes the all-Ce upper bound rather than inventing a formula. Structurally blind to: the chemical radiolysis channel, dose-rate effects, and the packaging environment (blister, N2) that sets how much water is present to radiolyse.
